adjudication_records.issue_text: tests/base/src/test/java/org/keycloak/tests/admin/group/GroupTest.java:155 — Reader thread is never joined, so the assertion can run before the reader records an in-flight exception, letting the test pass while the bug is still present.

tests/base/src/test/java/org/keycloak/tests/admin/group/GroupTest.java:139 — Nothing checks that the reader completed any request during the delete window (no start latch or iteration count), so on a loaded runner it may never overlap the deletes and passes without testing anything.

adjudication.rationale: In the newly added test `createMultiDeleteMultiReadMulti`, the reader thread is started with `new Thread(...).start()` and loops while `!deletedAll.get()`, but there is no synchronization (e.g., latch/barrier) or iteration counter to ensure the thread actually performs any `managedRealm.admin().groups().groups(...)` call before deletions finish and `deletedAll` is set to true. If the thread is scheduled late, it can do zero reads, `caughtExceptions` stays empty, and the assertion passes without exercising the intended concurrent read/delete window.

adjudication_records.issue_text: tests/base/src/test/java/org/keycloak/tests/admin/group/GroupTest.java:147 — The reader thread only catches Exception, so Errors are lost, and it is never stopped if a delete throws, which leaks a thread that keeps hitting the realm after the test fails.

adjudication.rationale: In the added test `createMultiDeleteMultiReadMulti`, a new reader thread is started (`new Thread(...).start()`) and is only stopped when `deletedAll.set(true)` is reached after the delete loop. If any deletion (or earlier code) throws and the test fails before setting `deletedAll`, the thread will keep running and continue calling `managedRealm.admin().groups().groups(...)`, leaking activity beyond the test. Also, the thread only catches `Exception`, so `Error`/`AssertionError` in that thread would not be captured in `caughtExceptions` and therefore wouldn’t fail the test as intended.

There is no synchronization/barrier to ensure the reader actually performs any `groups()` calls during the deletion window, so it may run zero or only a few iterations depending on scheduling. Also, the test never `join()`s the reader thread before asserting, so the assertion can occur before the reader has meaningfully exercised the race. This makes the test non-deterministic and it can pass without reproducing the intended NPE.

adjudication_records.issue_text: tests/base/src/test/java/org/keycloak/tests/admin/group/GroupTest.java:146 — Catching only Exception misses Errors (e.g. AssertionError/OOM) in the thread, which die silently without failing the test.

adjudication.rationale: In the newly added test `createMultiDeleteMultiReadMulti`, the spawned reader thread wraps its loop in `try { ... } catch (Exception e) { caughtExceptions.add(e); }`. If the thread throws an `Error` (e.g., `AssertionError`, `OutOfMemoryError`, etc.), it will not be caught, the thread can terminate, and the main test will still proceed to `assertThat(caughtExceptions, Matchers.empty())` and may pass. There is also no `join()`/uncaught-exception handler to surface such failures, so thread Errors can indeed die silently without failing the test.

adjudication_records.issue_text: tests/base/src/test/java/org/keycloak/tests/admin/group/GroupTest.java:157 — Test never asserts the reader completed at least one request concurrently with deletion, so a passing run proves nothing about the fixed getSubGroupsCount path.

adjudication_records.issue_text: tests/base/src/test/java/org/keycloak/tests/admin/group/GroupTest.java:153 — Groups created by the test are only removed in the happy path; a failure mid-creation or mid-deletion leaves up to 100 groups behind with no try/finally cleanup.

adjudication.rationale: In the newly added test `createMultiDeleteMultiReadMulti`, groups are created and tracked in `groupUuuids`, but there is no `try/finally` (or similar) to ensure cleanup if the test aborts early. A failure during the creation loop calls `fail(...)` immediately, leaving already-created groups behind. Likewise, the deletion loop has no exception handling; if `remove()` throws mid-loop, remaining groups won’t be removed. This matches the finding that up to 100 groups can be left behind on non-happy paths.
